claims.text: Warm AIHA relapsing after or refractory to glucocorticoids: rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV weekly for 4 weeks (alternatives 1000 mg on days 1 and 15, or 100 mg weekly x4).
claims.quote: In patients who relapse after glucocorticoid cessation or who are refractory to glucocorticoids, rituximab is usually used as a second-line drug. Many experts also add rituximab to first-line treatment, especially in severe cases (6). Three dosing regimens of rituximab are used in clinical practice. The standard dose is 375 mg/m² IV weekly for 4 weeks; this is the most commonly used and best-studied regimen. Alternatives include a fixed high dose of 1000 mg IV on day 1 and day 15 (2 doses, 2 weeks apart), which has been used in some randomized trials, and a low fixed dose of 100 mg IV weekly for 4 weeks

claims.text: Warm AIHA, refractory cases: IVIG, immunosuppressants (azathioprine, mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide), splenectomy;
claims.quote: For idiopathic warm antibody hemolytic anemia, glucocorticoids and, in refractory cases, rituximab, IVIG, immunosuppression (eg, with azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, or cyclophosphamide), or splenectomy

claims.text: IVIG has given temporary control of less severe but uncontrolled hemolysis.
claims.quote: For less severe but uncontrolled hemolysis, IVIG infusions have provided temporary control
avoidance of cold environments and other triggers of hemolysis may be all that is needed to prevent symptomatic anemia
For primary cold agglutinin disease, rituximab, sometimes with bendamustine, is commonly used

claims.text: glucocorticoids have limited effect and shouldn't be used.
claims.quote: glucocorticoids have limited effectiveness and should not be used as a treatment

claims.text: Sutimlimab (classical complement inhibitor) for severe or symptomatic cold agglutinin anemia;
claims.quote: Complement inhibition with sutimlimab may be used in patients with severe anemia whose disease requires a more rapid response to therapy or in those with symptomatic anemia
